hero.statement: I build what runs <0>behind</0> the screens.
hero.intro: I build APIs, queues and integrations between systems that can't stop, like ERPs and marketplaces, with NestJS, RabbitMQ and Kubernetes. I study Computer Science at UNESC and, in my spare time, make games that run in the browser.

pipeline.eyebrow: Toy · my day job, in miniature
pipeline.caption: Orders come down from the marketplaces into SAP, and the way back carries the invoice status and the tracking to each of them. If either side fails, the message goes to the retry queue with backoff and, after the third retry, to the DLQ.
pipeline.hint: Click SAP or a marketplace to take it down.

about.title: I like systems that <0>can't stop</0>, and games that shouldn't end.
about.p1: I started out as an IT technician, building machines and supporting companies, and the love for hardware never left (no wonder my thesis has an ESP32 in it). These days I spend my time thinking about queues, idempotency and what happens to an order when the system on the other side answers 503.
about.p2: I like understanding things all the way down, which is why I also enjoy low-level languages, high-performance systems and any problem that looks simple until it hits production. Outside work, that turns into games: deterministic simulations, authoritative multiplayer and fully procedural worlds.
